title: Trust between strangers, and the Microsoft stack
brief: Your agent will call agents you do not own, and others will call yours. Identity, delegation, consent and the platform you run on shape what is possible. Decide how callers authenticate, what a credential request inside a task may do, and what Foundry and Agent Framework support.

blocks.caption: How A2A layers trust. A2A treats agents as standard enterprise applications and leaves identity to HTTP standards, where MCP defines its own OAuth profile [[r1]] [[r8]] [[r21]]
head: Layer
Rule
Consequence for design
rows: Transport
Production deployments MUST use HTTPS or TLS. Clients SHOULD verify the server certificate
No plain HTTP between agents, including in the same network
Identity
No user or client identity travels in the payload. Credentials are obtained out of band and sent on every request in HTTP headers or metadata
Delegation must be built from tokens, not message fields
Authentication
A server MUST authenticate every incoming request against the schemes declared in its card
A card that lists a scheme does not enforce it by itself
Authorization
Implementation-specific. It may consider skills, actions within tasks, data policies and OAuth scopes. Task listing, get, cancel and subscribe MUST be scoped to the caller
Check authorization before any database query that could reveal other callers' tasks
In-task authorization
An agent can move a task to `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED` and ask the client to fulfill a credential request, ideally out of band
The state alone authorizes nothing. Scope and lifetime are yours to define
Observability
Participate in distributed tracing with W3C Trace Context headers, log `taskId` and correlation ids, audit sensitive events
Fronting A2A servers with API management is highly recommended across organizations

blocks.title: Pick a security scheme for the card
blocks.prompt: Flip where the caller sits, whose authority the call carries and how many callers you serve.

options.name: API key
options.summary: A shared secret in a header, query or cookie.

options.name: OpenID Connect
options.summary: Discovery through the identity provider's metadata.

partner.why: A shared secret across organizations is hard to scope and rotate.

many.why: Key distribution and rotation do not scale.

tenant.why: Machine identities with scopes fit internal agents.

many.why: Standard token issuance scales and revokes centrally.

partner.why: Users sign in through their own provider.

user.why: The token carries the user's authority.

tenant.why: Reuse the enterprise identity provider and its discovery URL.

partner.why: Strong channel binding between known organizations.

user.why: A certificate says nothing about a user.

blocks.takeaway: A user in the loop points to authorization code. A service identity points to client credentials or mutual TLS. Keys are the cheapest and the hardest to scope.

blocks.caption: A2A on Microsoft platforms as of 2026-10-13
head: Capability
Foundry Agent Service
Microsoft Agent Framework
rows: Call a remote A2A agent

Tool type `a2a` targets A2A 1.0 and is generally available. `a2a_preview` targets 0.3 and is in preview. A project connection stores auth: `none`, `custom-keys`, `oauth2`, `user-entra-token`, `project-managed-identity` or `agentic-identity` [[r16]]
`A2AAgent` wraps a remote endpoint as an agent. .NET resolves the card with `A2ACardResolver`. Packages are prerelease [[r15]]
Expose your agent over A2A
Incoming A2A for v1.0: JSON-RPC only, text only, no streaming, requires the responses protocol, Entra auth only [[r17]]
.NET `MapA2AHttpJson`. Python `A2AExecutor`. Go has a provider package. Prerelease [[r14]]
Versions
Serves 1.0 and preview 0.3. With no `A2A-Version` header or `a2a-version` query value it serves 0.3. Header and query must agree or Foundry returns 400 [[r17]]
Not stated on the pages reviewed. Check the SDK release notes before relying on a version
Conversation state
Tasks and contexts are kept 60 days from the most recent write [[r17]]
The A2A `context_id` becomes the session id. If the remote restarts and loses state, context may be lost [[r14]] [[r12]]
Legacy
The Connected Agents tool is not available in the new Foundry Agent Service. Use the A2A tool [[r16]]
Agents as tools remain the in-process option [[r13]]

blocks.title: Failure modes and how to detect them

items.symptom: 401 or 403 when calling a Foundry agent over A2A with a valid Entra token
items.cause: The calling identity lacks the Foundry Agent Consumer role on the project or agent. The role goes to the principal's object id
items.fix: Assign the role at the narrowest scope that works. For OBO grant the user or a group, for service calls grant the agent identity, service principal or managed identity

items.cause: No version selector was sent, so Foundry served preview 0.3
items.fix: Send `A2A-Version: 1.0`, use the `agentCard/v1.0` URL, or the query value. Keep header and query consistent

items.symptom: A destructive step ran after the client replied to `AUTH_REQUIRED`
items.cause: The agent treated the state change or the credential as authorization for the operation
items.fix: The spec says the agent MUST NOT treat the state transition as authorization. Check the specific operation and scope after the credential arrives

items.symptom: A credential travelled through three agents and was reused
items.cause: In-band credential exchange across a chain of agents exposes it to each hop
items.fix: Prefer out-of-band delivery. If in-band, bind the credential to the originating agent and encrypt it for that agent

items.symptom: Conversation context vanished after two months or a restart
items.cause: Foundry's 60-day retention from the last write, or a remote agent that restarted without durable state
items.fix: Persist your own conversation summary and design for expiry. Reset the clock only by writing to the task

items: The agent MUST track the work as a Task, move it to `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED` and include a status message that explains the need, unless negotiated out of band.
Credentials SHOULD arrive out of band over a secure channel. If received that way, the agent SHOULD keep active streams open and MAY continue without a follow-up message.
A client that is itself an A2A agent can pass the request up by moving its own task to `AUTH_REQUIRED`, forming a chain.
Clients that lack a live stream risk missing the resume, so they should subscribe, register a webhook or poll.
Credentials obtained for one request MUST NOT be assumed to authorize later messages on the task unless the implementation, issuer or an extension says so [[r1]].

items.title: Foundry identity patterns for incoming A2A

items: Incoming A2A requires Microsoft Entra ID authentication. Key-based and anonymous access, even to the agent card, are not supported [[r17]].
On-behalf-of: the caller passes the end user's identity, so the agent can scope actions to that user's permissions.
Service identity: the caller authenticates as an agent identity, service principal or managed identity, which suits backend workflows where no user context is needed [[r17]].

To call a Foundry agent target with the A2A tool, use the target's A2A base path, `agentic-identity` auth and the audience `https://ai.azure.com`. To read a card that requires authentication, set `send_credentials_for_agent_card` to true [[r16]].
.NET hosting uses `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Hosting.A2A.AspNetCore` with `MapA2AHttpJson`, installed with `--prerelease`. The client package is `Microsoft.Agents.AI.A2A` [[r14]] [[r15]].
Python uses `pip install agent-framework-a2a --pre` for `A2AAgent` (client) and `A2AExecutor` (server, built on `a2a-sdk`) [[r14]] [[r15]].
`A2AAgent` is a transport-level wrapper. Whatever tools the remote agent uses stay on the remote side and are invisible to your code [[r15]].
For long calls, `AllowBackgroundResponses` returns a continuation token you can poll or use to reconnect a stream [[r15]].

blocks.title: Preview and GA labels, verified 2026-10-13
blocks.md: The Foundry `a2a` tool and A2A 1.0 are generally available. `a2a_preview` and A2A 0.3 are in preview. The Agent Framework A2A packages are prerelease. Say the label and the date whenever you recommend one [[r16]] [[r17]] [[r14]].

quiz.q: A Foundry agent task receives writes on day 0, day 20 and day 70 and none afterward. Counting from day 0, on which day is retention scheduled to end?
quiz.hint: Foundry retains tasks and contexts for 60 days from the most recent write
quiz.explain: Each write resets the 60-day clock. The last write was on day 70, so retention ends on day 130. Counting from day 0 or day 20 is wrong because those writes were superseded.

quiz.q: A client calls a Foundry agent's A2A endpoint with no version header and receives 0.3-shaped payloads that its 1.0 parser rejects. What is the fix?
options: Switch the binding to gRPC, which always returns 1.0
Enable streaming on the agent so it upgrades the protocol
Disable the Entra token check on the agent so the request is routed to the 1.0 handler instead of the default one
Send `A2A-Version: 1.0`, or use the v1.0 agent card URL, so Foundry serves 1.0
quiz.explain: With no selector Foundry serves preview 0.3. Version 1.0 is chosen by header, query value or the version-specific card URL. For v1.0 Foundry supports only JSON-RPC and no streaming, and authentication is unrelated to the version.

quiz.q: A task enters `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED` before a destructive step. The client obtains a token and sends the next message. What may the agent assume?
options: That the state transition itself authorized the destructive step
That any credential received in this state authorizes every later message on the task
Nothing automatically: the agent must check that the credential and scope cover that specific operation
That the client's earlier authentication is void and the task must restart
quiz.explain: The spec says agents MUST NOT treat the `AUTH_REQUIRED` transition as authorization, and a credential obtained then MUST NOT be assumed to cover later messages unless the implementation, issuer or an extension defines that. Restarting is not required.

quiz.q: Match each Microsoft A2A item to what it is.

pairs.r: Calls remote agents using A2A 1.0, generally available

pairs.l: Incoming A2A on a Foundry agent (v1.0)
pairs.r: JSON-RPC only, text only, no streaming, Entra auth
Python server-side adapter built on the A2A SDK

quiz.explain: These pairings come from the Foundry and Agent Framework docs verified on 2026-10-13. The Foundry incoming limits apply to v1.0, and the Agent Framework packages are prerelease.

takeaways: A2A leaves identity to HTTP: authenticate every request, scope every task operation to the caller and keep identity out of the payload.
Pick the scheme by caller location, whose authority the call carries and caller count.
`AUTH_REQUIRED` hands a credential job to the client. The state itself authorizes nothing.
Foundry's `a2a` tool is GA for 1.0. Incoming A2A is JSON-RPC, text only and non-streaming, and defaults to 0.3 without a version selector.
Agent Framework A2A packages are prerelease. `A2AAgent` hides the remote agent's tools.
